Tuesday, January 28, 2020  7:00 PM  Council Chamber

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstatesCA.gov
  and during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's
  web site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on
  PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG
  Dapplegray Elementary Student Council

  City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JANUARY 28, 2020

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Dapplegray Elementary Student Council led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman ‘

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development and Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Services Coordinator Cynthia Morquecho
  Acting City Clerk Carol Corea

4.  CERMONIAL ITEMS

NONE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

COUNCIL MEMBER  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by,  COUNCIL  MEMBER
ZERUNYAN,

THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A - E AS
RECOMMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 14, 2020

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JANUARY 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62365 THROUGH 62428 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $347,229.66 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 010420 THROUGH
  010620 IN THE AMOUNT OF $112,032.70 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $459,262.36 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT – DECEMBER 2019

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JANUARY 28, 2020
   RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPOT – DECEMBER 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Carmelo Sorce, Cal Water provided an update on the Palos Verdes Peninsula Pipeline
Project.

Gracie McGovern, Chadwick School Sustainability Council, addressed the City Council
to suggest green initiatives, including a ban on gas-powered leaf blowers and single-use
plastics.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  2020-2021 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT FUNDS

  APPROVED RESOLUTION NO. 2449 AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF A
  CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE
  PROGRAM FOR FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS RAMP AND
  SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE
  PROGRAM AND CONDITIONS ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL
  2, 2014 IN THE AMOUNT OF APPROXIMATELY $29,406.

  AYES:  Mitchell, Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman, Schmitz
  ABSENT:  None

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSAL FOR PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR 2020
  STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  APPROVED THE TASK ORDER WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING, TO
  PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR DESIGN,
  CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND OBSERVATION FOR SERVICES
  FOR THE 2020 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT IN A NOT-TO-
  EXCEED AMOUNT OF $53,820.

  AYES:  Mitchell, Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman, Schmitz
  ABSENT:  None

B.  DRAFT 2020 MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN

  RECEIVED AND FILED

ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING

C.  SPONSORSHIP PROGRAM

  ADOPTED THE SPONSORSHIP PROGRAM AS REVISED TO BE
  IMPLEMENTED FOR 2020 CITY EVENTS.

  AYES:  Mitchell, Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman, Schmitz
  ABSENT:  None

RECONVENE TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 28, 2020
 9.  OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Board of Directors met last Thursday (January 23) and that SBCCOG
received a $740,000 grant from Los Angeles County to develop projects to help those
experiencing homelessness. One of the SBCCOG’s projects will be working with Silver
Nest, which is an organization that assists with matching people for home sharing.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that SBCCOG’s Senior Services Working Group met
today and there was a report by the Angeles Emeralds, a Cannabis Awareness Group
working to inform the public that there are only a small number of sales outlets that are
certified and test their product for pureness. In addition, Assembly Bill 228 which would
legalize hemp CBD without any testing may be put forward again. The Angeles Emeralds
Group is working to inform the public about this bill.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that the Senate Bill 50 by Senator Wiener is
now under consideration by the Senate Rules Committee, which will give it a better
chance to pass and move to the Senate floor. The Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) and other organizations have written letters regarding SB 50 to
State Legislators. He also stated that SCAG received a letter from the Department of
Housing and Community Development (HCD) confirming that SCAG’s Regional Housing
Need Allocation (RHNA) methodology was correct and meets the statutory objectives. He
further stated that he is working with his colleagues to draft a white paper for workable
solutions to the state’s housing needs.

MAYOR SCHMITZ stated that she signed a letter expressing the City’s opposition to SB
50 that was sent to the bill’s author as well as local state representatives.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF provided information regarding upcoming events including
the Legislative Breakfast at the Nakano Theater in Torrance on Friday, January 31 and
The U.S. Census Roundtable on Monday, February 3 at the Redondo Beach Performing
Arts Center. She added that the SBCCOG General Assembly is Thursday, March 19 in
Carson and registration is required.

MAYOR SCHMITZ stated that the City’s Community Roundup will be held on Tuesday,
February 4 at 6:30 pm in the Council Chamber. Items to be discussed are: the new State
Housing Legislation, Clean Power Alliance, General Plan Update, Capital Projects, and
Emergency Operation and Hazard Mitigation Plan.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN stated that the Holiday Parade Subcommittee met
yesterday and discussed ways to generate a large crowd on Deep Valley Drive, including
the possibility of pop-up restaurants or food trucks. He further stated that there was
discussion on how to get the word out about including more local school floats.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  A.  2020 POLICY DEVELOPMENT/STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION –
  SUGGESTED ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

The following are topics to be added to the 2020 Policy Development/Strategic Planning
Session:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 28, 2020
   ·  COUNCILMEMBER MITCHELL – New Housing and ADU laws; RHNA allocation;
  2020 Census; Open Space.
  ·  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN – Sustainability in Building Standards; Public
  Works options for sustainability.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:58 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting. The next adjourned
City Council meeting will be the Community Roundup on Tuesday, February 4, 2020 at
6:30 pm.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carol Corea  Greg Grammer
Acting City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 28, 2020
